title: Wet Well Volume — Minimum Cycle Time

V.description: Minimum effective wet well volume (between start and stop levels)

Q_pump.description: Pump flow rate (for single pump; for multiple, use the pump that cycles)

applicability: T_cycle typically 6–15 min for motors < 150 kW, 15–30 min for larger. Maximum cycling frequency ≈ 6–10 starts/hour for standard motors. VFD-driven pumps have no cycling limit.

title: Minimum Submergence (HI 9.8)

S.description: Minimum submergence above bell entrance rim

Fr_D.description: Froude number at bell entrance = V_bell / √(g × D_bell)

applicability: V_bell = Q/(π/4 × D_bell²). Target V_bell ≤ 1.7 m/s. Inadequate submergence causes surface vortices and air entrainment. For approach flow with swirl or non-uniformity, increase S by 25–50%.

title: Standby Generator Sizing

P_motor_running.description: Running power of each motor operating simultaneously

P_starting.description: Additional power for starting the largest motor (6× FLA for across-the-line)

1.25.description: Derating factor for altitude, temperature, and margin

applicability: Generator must handle the running load PLUS the starting surge of the next motor to start. Soft starts or VFDs reduce starting power significantly. Include station auxiliary loads (lighting, HVAC, controls).

title: Buoyancy Check — Below-Grade Structure

FS_buoyancy.description: Factor of safety against flotation (≥ 1.1 minimum)

W_structure.description: Total weight of structure (concrete, equipment, permanent fill)

V_displaced.description: Volume of structure below maximum groundwater level

applicability: Check for empty station condition (no water in wet well, no equipment). If FS < 1.1, add weight (thicker base slab) or install permanent dewatering/anchor system.

title: Ventilation Rate for Pump Room

ACH.description: Air changes per hour (12–20 for pump rooms, 30+ for confined/below-grade)

applicability: Heat dissipation from motors is the primary driver for dry-pit pump rooms. Check: Q_vent × ρ_air × c_p × ΔT ≥ motor heat rejection. Supplemental cooling needed if ΔT > 10°C.

title: Crane Capacity for Pump Removal

W_pipe_section.description: Weight of heaviest pipe/valve section to be removed

FS_crane.description: Crane safety factor (minimum 1.25 on rated load)

applicability: Overhead bridge crane or monorail. Clear height above equipment for rigging (typically 1.5–2.5 m above highest component). Hook reach must cover all equipment positions and the equipment hatch/door.

title: Annual Energy Cost

P_brake.description: Average brake power at operating point

applicability: For variable-demand stations, calculate weighted average of flow/head conditions. Include demand charges ($/kW) based on peak power. Energy cost typically 50–80% of total life-cycle cost.

title: Present Worth Life-Cycle Cost
applicability: Compare alternatives (e.g., larger pipe + smaller pump vs. smaller pipe + larger pump) on present-worth basis. Typical analysis period: 20–50 years. Include major equipment replacement at mid-life.
